{"headline":"Your neuroticism will probably head down","explanation":"The model gives your neuroticism a 51% chance of moving by half a standard deviation or more between 23 and 39: 18% for a rise and 32% for a fall. Its single best guess is that you stay close to the 9th percentile. The biggest single push is upwards, from the natural drift towards average, but the other factors together outweigh it. Most of the uncertainty is simply time, because over 16 years people move around more than they expect.","drivers":[{"label":"Natural drift toward average","effect":"raises","plain":"Scores far from the middle tend to drift back towards it over the years, and yours starts below average."},{"label":"Maturation, age 23→39","effect":"lowers","plain":"Most people grow calmer with age, especially through their twenties and thirties."},{"label":"Long-term relationship","effect":"lowers","plain":"A first long-term relationship goes with slightly lower neuroticism on average, and the size used here is an estimate."}],"caveat":"Life events are partly chosen by personality in the first place, so their effects here are associations, not guarantees."}
